messages:
oncall-bot: Pager — HIGH: gpu-pool eu-west-1 saturated; autoscaler failed to increase beyond configured max_replicas, queue growth detected.
oncall-bot: summary: queue_len=11,240, outstanding_rps=420, autoscaler attempted target=64 but max_replicas=64 (limit hit), throttling started ~1718765400.

sara (oncall): I'm on it. pulling metrics now. any customer-facing alerts currently?

linda (customer-ops): CS: two customers reporting 503s (acme-inc, beta-app). I've acknowledged and sent initial note.

mike (eng-sre): Looking at controller logs — scale attempts failing with quota errors. Snippet: 
```
2024-06-14T12:15:02Z autoscaler-controller: attempt_scale to 64 -> error: quota_exceeded (provider)
2024-06-14T12:15:10Z runtime: enqueue_latency.p95=8.2s, inflight=1240
```

julia (infra): Confirmed provider-side quota at account level for eu-west-1. Node provisioning lag ~8m right now. Opening cloud ticket.

kyle (runtime): Runtime note: queue draining slow because a subset of streaming jobs have very long token lengths and are occupying KV caches. Suggest immediate soft-eviction of low-priority/free-tier jobs.

sara (oncall): Proposed mitigation plan (short):
1) enable emergency-burst (reserved local nodes) for 10-20m
2) apply per-customer throttle for free tier to reduce enqueue rate
3) route low-tier traffic to smaller model variant (redwood-medium) as fallback
4) watch for provider limit bump and remove burst when stable
Anyone object to that order?

mike (eng-sre): +1 to throttles and fallback. I'll prepare scale-limit bump commands but need infra approval to touch provider quotas. Command I'll run for local pool if approved: 
```
kubectl apply -f emergency-scaleup.yaml --namespace=redwood-runtime
```

julia (infra): I've opened ticket CLD-9821 with cloud provider for quota bump; they estimated ~20m. Meanwhile we can spin up dedicated nodes in our spare reserved capacity. I'll coordinate ops.

kyle (runtime): Rolling a route policy change now to divert free-tier to redwood-medium (lower token cost) — doing canary first. Policy: 
```
route.set(policy="fallback-free", if_tier=="free") -> model=redwood-medium
```

sara (oncall): Applying emergency-burst (allocating 8 G4s from dedicated pool) now. Executing throttle rule for free-tier at 50% of baseline.

oncall-bot: Action: emergency-burst enabled by sara at 1718765605 (added 8 GPUs, dedicated pool=eu-west-1-burst).

linda (customer-ops): CS update: notified affected customers, offering 2% credit for time impacted. Beta-app reports partial recovery.

mike (eng-sre): Autoscaler telemetry shows successful scale after burst: scaled_to=72, no further quota errors in controller.

kyle (runtime): Observability: p95 latency improved from 8.2s -> 1.9s after fallback policy and burst. Enqueue rate steady.

sara (oncall): Closing active pager — queue length trending down. We still have followups. Action items: 
- Increase autoscaler max_replicas for eu-west-1 to 200 (temporary limit)
- Implement tenant-level soft-throttles (free tier) in policy engine
- Alert rule: sustained enqueue growth > 1k/min for 3m -> page oncall
- Postmortem + action assignment (INC-2718)

mike (eng-sre): I'll own autoscaler max_replicas bump and alert rule (#1 and #3). Will coordinate with infra for provider quota changes.

julia (infra): I'll own implementation of tenant throttles in infra and coord with kyle for runtime enforcement (#2). Also follow up on CLD-9821 with provider.

linda (customer-ops): I'll own customer comms and post-incident outreach.

sara (oncall): TL;DR: mitigations (burst + fallback + throttles) restored service and avoided sustained SLO breach. No data loss, some 503s observed and customers notified. Created INC-2718 for postmortem.

deploy-bot: Deployment: emergency-burst applied successfully. commit=abc123def, started_by=sara, duration=00:02:30

sara (oncall): Thanks. I'll draft the postmortem and schedule a review at 10:00 UTC tomorrow. :thumbsup:

kyle (runtime): +1. Also proposing a medium-term feature: model-autoscale-weighting to bias autoscaler toward spinning up cheaper/smaller variants first.

mike (eng-sre): Add to INC-2718 backlog. Good work everyone — leaving notes in playbook and closing thread.
